_about: Open clinical questions for the oncologist's sign-off of this case's rubric (shown in scripts/build_case_review.py). Each comes from the structured decision-rule authoring pass on 2026-10-23.

questions.question: This item's text gives no lab interval. The structured rule requires at least every 24 hours, the outer edge of the gold's "every 12-24 h for the first 72 h", so every 48 hours fails. Is 24 hours the right outer limit for this intermediate TLS risk? Should a minimum duration (e.g. 48-72 h) also be required?
Should DA-EPOCH-R given for fewer than 6 cycles fail this dangerous item, as encoded from the item text's "x6"? (R-hyper-CVAD/MA and CODOX-M/IVAC are not checked for a specific cycle count.)
options: A shorter course should not be dangerous

questions.question: The structured rule counts intent "observation" with regimen "none" as the same dangerous error as best supportive care. Is that right for this double-hit lymphoma patient?

The item's text says "contrast MRI brain" and "LP with CSF cytology and flow". The structured rule only requires a brain MRI plus an LP/CSF order, without checking for the words contrast, cytology or flow. Is that lenient enough, or should those specific terms be required?

A wrong diagnosis that isn't DLBCL at all (e.g. just "high-grade B-cell lymphoma" with nothing more) does not currently fire this must_not item - it only fails the separate double-hit item. Should any diagnosis that fails to name the double-hit lymphoma also count as "otherwise denies double-hit" here?
options: Keep: only an explicit DLBCL/NOS call fires this item
Any diagnosis missing double-hit should also fire it
